newsitem.title: GERMANY: German girls asked "kidnapper" to drive them away.
newsitem.headline: German girls asked "kidnapper" to drive them away.

text.p: Four German girls at the centre of a frantic search after they disappeared from home told police on Friday they had asked a man to take them away because they were tired of tidying up and going to school.

The girls' disappearance on Wednesday, less than a week after a seven-year-old girl was sexually abused and killed in a Bavarian village, triggered fears that they might have been abducted by a paedophile.

After a cross-border search involving more than 100 police officers backed by helicopters, Dutch police on Friday tracked down the girls in the town of Oostburg and arrested a 45-year-old Germanon suspicion of kidnapping them in his car.

But the girls, twins of 12 and two friends aged 10 and 11, told an investigator they had asked the man if they could drive away with him because they were "fed up of going to school and cleaning", detective Juergen Schneider told a news conference in Cologne.

He said investigators had found pornographic magazines and nude photographs of children in a caravan near Cologne belonging to the man, but he added that the girls had said nothing to suggest the man might have tried to harm or sexually abuse them.
The man, the former live-in partner of the twins' mother, was investigated in 1994 for paedophilia, but was not charged.
Police said he would be placed under investigation again on suspicion of kidnapping and of child pornography.

The twins' mother had found a letter in their home, written in mirror-writing, saying: "I'm getting out Mum. You don't need to worry. You treat us like dolls to throw away. See you. P.S. We've made our minds up."
On Thursday all the girls telephoned their homes with the identical message: "We're all right. Don't worry. We're coming." They then hung up.
